---
title: "Pre-trend benchmarking demo"
output: html_document
---

Load the updated package (0.2.2.9008 or later).

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE)
library(did)
library(dml.sensemakr)
```

1. Fit the original DiD model.

```{r}
data("mpdta", package = "did")
fit <- did::att_gt(
  data = mpdta, yname = "lemp", tname = "year",
  idname = "countyreal", gname = "first.treat", xformla = ~ lpop,
  panel = TRUE, est_method = "dr", control_group = "nevertreated",
  bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE, compute_inffunc = TRUE
)
```

2. Use the source nuisance-fitting procedure (previously called Option 2).

```{r}
m <- dml_from_did(fit, group = 2007, time = 2007, method = "replicate")
```

3. Benchmark against the 2005-to-2006 pre-trend on the same units.

```{r}
b <- did_pretrend_bounds(
  m, pre_period = c(2005, 2006), k = c(0, 0.5, 1, 2),
  type = "bias", level = 0.975
)
b
```

`k = 1` allows post-treatment bias as large as the pre-period placebo ATT in
absolute value. Change `type` to `"scaled"` to adjust for the sensitivity-scale
ratio. `theta.minus` / `theta.plus` are point bounds; `lwr` / `upr` include
sampling uncertainty. The selected level gives at least 95% asymptotic
coverage of both population endpoints for each fixed `k` under the assumptions.

To use DML instead, change step 2 to
`dml_from_did(fit, 2007, 2007, method = "dml", dml_args = list(dirty.tuning = TRUE))`.
Omit `dirty.tuning` or set it to `FALSE` for the adapter's default clean tuning.

Interpretation requires no pre-period causal effect and the chosen pre/post
bias restriction. For positive `k`, regular delta inference requires a nonzero
population placebo ATT and can be unreliable near zero.
